subject.title: TUI /sessions list: gateway-injected inbound metadata block used as session title (shows 'untrusted metadata' for all sessions)

question: Should maintainers adopt/rebase the open fork PR, replace it with a fresh narrow same-repo fix, or close that fork PR before queueing another automated fix for this issue?
rationale: The bug shape and fix boundary are clear, but an open conflicting fork PR still uses closing syntax for this issue, so ClawSweeper should not create another fix PR until maintainers choose the branch path.

options.title: Replace With Fresh Narrow Fix
options.body: Close or supersede the stale conflicting fork branch and land a focused same-repo fix covering metadata stripping plus sync and async displayName hydration.

options.title: Adopt Or Rebase Fork PR
options.body: Have a maintainer or contributor update the fork PR to current main, add missing coverage and proof, then review it as the landing candidate.

options.title: Keep Waiting On Fork PR
options.body: Leave this issue blocked on the existing fork PR despite its stale base and conflict state.

recommendation.title: Replace With Fresh Narrow Fix
recommendation.body: Close or supersede the stale conflicting fork branch and land a focused same-repo fix covering metadata stripping plus sync and async displayName hydration.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle has the strongest recent routing signal in the Gateway session-list performance and TUI picker history, and prior ClawSweeper review already routed the branch choice to maintainer handling.
